known_blockers: the production application adapter is not wired to the additive q-label and text-entity compatibility contract
legacy numeric id and stable note/entity identity are only proven with synthetic mappings, not a full live mapping freeze
current production API has no expected revision or idempotency contract and hard-deletes notes
shared identity dependency mapping is not fully frozen and verified
manual write authentication, CSRF and least-privilege production role are not evidenced
production PostgreSQL topology, off-VM backup and restore evidence do not yet exist
application repository production-authority governance gate remains open

nonproduction_rehearsal.environment: loopback PostgreSQL dev/test on a non-production port
covered: S2 verification then return to S1 with no formal write
first formal mutation and S2-to-S3 authority revision in one transaction
text Q label, text theme id, nullable title and legacy raw timestamp compatibility
least-privilege writer, reader and unit-specific controller roles
live SQLite schema and file hashes unchanged

state_contract.S0: SQLite is the only authority; PostgreSQL use is dev/test or offline rehearsal only
state_contract.S1: production structure, backup, identity mapping and backfill are ready while SQLite remains the only writer
state_contract.S2: short cutover fence; SQLite mutation paths are fenced and PostgreSQL accepts classified verification writes only
state_contract.S3: first durable formal PostgreSQL business write exists; PostgreSQL is the only authority and SQLite is not a direct rollback target
state_contract.S4: observation passed; legacy SQLite mutation path is permanently fenced or removed

uncertain_response_rule: If absence of a durable PostgreSQL business commit cannot be proven, classify the unit as S3 and reconcile by stable operation identity; never retry against SQLite.
reconciliation: stable note key and legacy id mapping uniqueness

recovery.S0_S1: abandon the PostgreSQL candidate without changing SQLite authority
recovery.S2_without_formal_write: restore SQLite writer only after stop-write, watermark, audit and human approval prove no required PostgreSQL write exists
recovery.S2_uncertain_or_S3: forward repair PostgreSQL, roll application code only if schema-compatible, or restore to a side environment and selectively repair production
recovery.S4: legacy SQLite is an audit baseline; reverse migration requires a separately approved migration
